steps.intent: As humanitarian co-penholder alongside Germany and Kuwait, Belgium's primary objective is to halt the devastating military campaign in north-west Syria, protect over three million vulnerable civilians, and safeguard critical civilian infrastructure and humanitarian access under international humanitarian law. The most difficult negotiating point is the counter-terrorism exemption in paragraph 2; the Russian Federation insists on unrestricted military operations against Hayat Tahrir al-Sham and opposes binding ceasefire dates, while we maintain that counter-terrorism operations cannot serve as a pretext to bypass international humanitarian law and indiscriminately target civilian populations.

Add at the end of the paragraph: ', in full accordance with the United Nations guiding principles of humanitarian emergency assistance and with full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic, in coordination with the Syrian Government;'

Equatorial Guinea.change: Reaffirming its strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic, and stressing that this must be respected in all circumstances and actions taken by the Council,

Ensure clear, robust and unambiguous exemption for military operations against all Security Council-designated terrorist groups, notably Hayat Tahrir al-Sham and Al-Qaida affiliates, so that counter-terrorism efforts are not hindered while ensuring the protection of civilians.
Call for intensified coordination and dialogue among all relevant actors, in particular the Astana guarantors, to preserve de-escalation arrangements and prevent further confrontation.

Russian Federation.change: Replace with wording acknowledging and welcoming the unilateral ceasefire announced by the Syrian armed forces with the support of the Russian Federation on 31 August 2019, rather than imposing an artificial deadline that undermines ongoing de-escalation efforts.

Delete the qualifying clause 'while underscoring that all measures taken to combat terrorism must strictly adhere to international humanitarian law' or ensure it cannot be exploited as a pretext to constrain legitimate counter-terrorism operations against Council-designated terrorist groups, notably Hayat Tahrir al-Sham, which controls the vast majority of Idlib.

Add explicit condemnation of the systematic shelling, rocket attacks, and provocations carried out by Hayat Tahrir al-Sham and affiliated terrorist groups against nearby civilian settlements and the Hmeimim airbase from within the de-escalation zone.
Reaffirm that the ultimate objective remains the full restoration of the sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic across all its internationally recognized territory.

messages.China: China attaches great importance to the humanitarian situation in Syria, but any action taken by the Council must fully respect the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. The Council cannot turn a blind eye to the reality that Idlib is dominated by Council-designated terrorist organizations that continually launch attacks against civilians and military targets. The draft text must avoid double standards on counter-terrorism, refrain from constraining legitimate operations against terrorists, and ensure humanitarian assistance is conducted in close coordination with the Syrian Government.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire fully supports the draft resolution presented by Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait, which addresses the dire and deteriorating humanitarian situation in north-west Syria. The protection of civilians, respect for international humanitarian law, and unimpeded humanitarian access are urgent imperatives that require decisive action by the Council. We encourage all Council members to work in a spirit of compromise and unity to ensure the adoption of this vital humanitarian measure.
messages.Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republic expresses its full support for the draft resolution presented by Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait. Given the catastrophic humanitarian situation in north-west Syria and the massive displacement of civilians, an immediate cessation of hostilities and strict adherence to international humanitarian law are urgent imperatives. We urge all Council members to unite behind this humanitarian initiative to protect innocent lives and ensure unimpeded humanitarian access.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea shares deep concern over the acute humanitarian suffering of civilians in north-west Syria and supports all genuine efforts to alleviate their plight. However, it is essential that the Security Council act with one voice and avoid division, ensuring that counter-terrorism measures against designated terrorist entities are not undermined while upholding international humanitarian law. We urge the penholders to consult closely with all Council members, particularly the permanent members, to bridge differences and achieve a consensual text.
messages.France: France fully supports the draft resolution presented by Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait, which addresses the intolerable humanitarian catastrophe in north-west Syria. The ongoing offensive by the Syrian regime and its allies in Idlib has caused unacceptable civilian suffering and the destruction of essential infrastructure, including hospitals and schools. While we remain resolute in the fight against terrorism, counter-terrorism operations cannot be used as a pretext to violate international humanitarian law, and we urge all Council members to adopt this vital humanitarian text without delay.
messages.Germany: As a co-penholder alongside Belgium and Kuwait, Germany fully supports the draft text as circulated. The catastrophic humanitarian situation in north-west Syria and the plight of over three million civilians in Idlib demand an immediate cessation of hostilities and unhindered humanitarian access. We emphasize that counter-terrorism operations cannot justify blatant violations of international humanitarian law or the relentless targeting of civilians, schools, and hospitals.
messages.Indonesia: Indonesia fully supports the draft resolution submitted by the humanitarian co-penholders, Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait, as an urgent and necessary response to alleviate the severe humanitarian suffering in north-west Syria. We stress that the protection of civilians and unhindered humanitarian access must remain paramount, and that all counter-terrorism measures must strictly comply with international humanitarian law. Indonesia urges all Council members to engage constructively and prioritize the lives of millions of innocent civilians, preserving Council unity behind this critical humanitarian initiative.
messages.Kuwait: As a co-sponsor and co-penholder alongside Belgium and Germany, Kuwait fully supports the text as drafted. The draft strikes an urgent and necessary balance by demanding an immediate cessation of hostilities to protect over three million civilians in Idlib while clarifying that counter-terrorism measures must strictly adhere to international humanitarian law. We urge all Council members to demonstrate unity in addressing this dire humanitarian catastrophe and adopt the resolution without delay.
messages.Peru: Peru expresses its full support for the draft resolution presented by Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait. Given the catastrophic humanitarian situation in north-west Syria and the massive displacement of civilians, an immediate cessation of hostilities and unhindered humanitarian access are imperative. We commend the penholders for crafting a balanced text that firmly upholds international humanitarian law and the protection of civilians, while acknowledging legitimate counter-terrorism efforts.
messages.Poland: Poland expresses its full support for the draft resolution presented by Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait. The catastrophic humanitarian situation in north-west Syria requires the Security Council to act decisively to demand an immediate cessation of hostilities and ensure unhindered humanitarian access. We stand ready to vote in favour of the text as drafted and urge all Council members to support this vital humanitarian initiative.
messages.Russian Federation: The draft in its current form is unacceptable as it attempts to shield terrorists in Idlib under a humanitarian pretext while ignoring the unilateral ceasefire declared on 31 August. Idlib cannot remain a safe haven for Hayat Tahrir al-Sham and other Council-designated terrorist entities holding the local civilian population hostage. Unless the text unequivocally recognizes the sovereign right of Syria to eradicate terrorism and reflects the actual reality on the ground, the Russian Federation will not support it.
messages.South Africa: South Africa commends the co-penholders for their dedicated efforts to address the alarming humanitarian situation in north-west Syria and to ensure the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure. We support the call for an immediate cessation of hostilities while upholding international humanitarian law in all counter-terrorism operations. We encourage the penholders to continue constructive engagement with all Council members to forge unity and ensure that Council action complements the UN-led political process under resolution 2254 (2015).
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports this draft resolution and commends Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait for their tireless work as humanitarian co-penholders. Given the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Idlib caused by the ongoing offensive by the Syrian regime and its Russian allies, an immediate cessation of hostilities is urgent and indispensable. We urge all Council members to support this text without delay and reject any attempts to weaken its protections for civilians and humanitarian infrastructure.
messages.United States of America: The United States strongly supports the draft resolution put forward by Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait to immediately halt the devastating military offensive by the Syrian regime and the Russian Federation in north-west Syria. The Council must act urgently to protect more than three million civilians in Idlib and put an end to relentless strikes on medical facilities, schools, and civilian infrastructure. We appreciate the penholders' balanced and principled work and urge all Council members to vote in favor of this critical humanitarian text without dilution.

before.Belgium:
I have the honour to speak on behalf of the co-penholders of the humanitarian file on Syria: Germany, Kuwait and my own country, Belgium.

For months, the eyes of the world have been turned to north-west Syria, where more than three million civilians are trapped in an escalating nightmare. Since late April, military operations have killed more than one thousand civilians, destroyed vital civilian infrastructure, including dozens of hospitals and schools, and displaced more than half a million people, many of them multiple times. The humanitarian catastrophe unfolding in Idlib is simply unacceptable.

As humanitarian co-penholders, our objective has always been purely humanitarian: to alleviate civilian suffering and ensure the protection of innocent people caught in the crossfire. The draft resolution before us today demands an immediate cessation of hostilities in Idlib to avert further catastrophe and to allow safe, unhindered and sustained humanitarian access. 

The text is balanced, realistic and strictly grounded in international humanitarian law. It explicitly recognizes the threat posed by Security Council-designated terrorist groups and permits military operations against them, while firmly reminding all parties that counter-terrorism efforts can never justify the violation of international humanitarian law or the collective punishment of an entire civilian population. 

The council cannot remain silent while millions of lives hang in the balance. We urge all members of the Council to put humanity first and to vote in favour of this draft resolution.
before.Russian Federation:
The Russian Federation will vote against the draft resolution submitted by Belgium, Germany and Kuwait.

We regret that the co-sponsors have stubbornly insisted on putting to a vote a text that is doomed to fail, despite our repeated warnings and constructive proposals. The authors of the draft chose confrontation over consensus, aiming not to genuinely resolve the humanitarian situation in Idlib, but rather to use humanitarian slogans for political ends and to shield terrorists who have taken millions of civilians hostage.

First, the draft completely ignores reality on the ground. A unilateral ceasefire introduced by the Syrian armed forces with the support of the Russian Federation has been in place since 31 August. Why impose an artificial new deadline for a cessation of hostilities when a ceasefire already exists and needs to be consolidated?

Second, the text attempts to tie the hands of those combating terrorism by introducing unacceptable caveats to counter-terrorist operations. Hayat Tahrir al-Sham, an Al-Qaida affiliate recognized as a terrorist organization by the Security Council, controls over 90 per cent of the Idlib de-escalation area. Terrorists cannot be granted a reprieve under the guise of humanitarian concern. There can be no compromise in the fight against terrorism, and Security Council resolutions clearly stipulate that terrorists must not find safe haven in Syria or anywhere else.

Our red lines and legitimate proposals were completely discarded by the co-penholders. For these reasons, the Russian Federation cannot support this draft resolution and will vote against it.

after.China:
(spoke in Chinese): China is deeply concerned about the humanitarian situation in Syria and sympathizes with the suffering of the Syrian people. We support the United Nations and the international community in scaling up humanitarian assistance to the Syrian people in accordance with the principles of humanity, neutrality and impartiality.

At the same time, China has consistently maintained that any action taken by the Security Council on the humanitarian issue in Syria must fully respect the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria, and heed the voice of the Syrian Government. 

The security and humanitarian issues in north-west Syria are fundamentally linked to the fact that terrorist organizations control the region. Groups such as Hayat Tahrir al-Sham, which is listed as a terrorist organization by the Security Council, have long controlled Idlib, launched repeated attacks against civilians and infrastructure, and taken local civilians hostage as human shields. Terrorism poses a serious threat to the peace and security of Syria and the region at large. The international community must adopt uniform standards, resolutely combat all terrorist groups designated by the Council, and not allow Idlib to become a breeding ground and safe haven for terrorists. Counter-terrorism efforts must be carried out in a coordinated and effective manner, in accordance with international law and relevant Council resolutions.

China actively participated in the consultations on the draft resolution. We, together with other Council members, proposed constructive amendments, including on effectively addressing the threat of terrorism and respecting Syria’s sovereignty, in an effort to reach consensus. We regret that the sponsors ignored these reasonable concerns and insisted on pushing for a vote when parties remained sharply divided. Forcing a vote on a draft resolution that lacks consensus will only undermine Council unity and does not help improve the situation on the ground. For those reasons, China voted against the draft resolution.

China reiterates that a political solution is the only viable way out of the Syrian crisis. We call on all parties to adhere to the Syrian-led and Syrian-owned principle, advance a comprehensive political process in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015), support the mediation efforts of Special Envoy Pedersen, and promote the early launch and substantive work of the Constitutional Committee, so as to achieve lasting peace, stability, and development in Syria.
after.Equatorial Guinea:
I have taken the floor to explain the vote of the delegation of the Republic of Equatorial Guinea on the draft resolution presented by the co-penholders (S/2019/756).

Equatorial Guinea remains deeply alarmed by the critical humanitarian situation in north-west Syria, particularly in Idlib governorate, where millions of innocent civilians continue to suffer the devastating consequences of violence, displacement and the destruction of vital civilian infrastructure. We firmly uphold that the protection of civilians and the unhindered delivery of humanitarian assistance are fundamental obligations under international humanitarian law that must be respected by all parties, without exception.

At the same time, my delegation reiterates its unwavering commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. We also recognize the legitimate duty to combat terrorism and terrorist organizations designated by this Council, whose presence and activities continue to pose a grave threat to the security and stability of the country and the region. Counter-terrorism operations, however, must be conducted in strict compliance with international humanitarian law and with maximum precautions to protect the civilian population.

Equatorial Guinea chose to abstain in the vote today because our delegation has consistently advocated for unity and consensus within the Security Council, especially on matters of an exclusively humanitarian nature. We deeply regret that, despite the tireless efforts made during consultations, the Council remains divided and was once again subjected to a vote on a text where positions were fundamentally irreconcilable and the outcome was already known in advance. We do not believe that persistent polarization and division among Council members contribute in any meaningful way to relieving the suffering of the Syrian people on the ground. 

Rather than engaging in confrontation and bringing draft resolutions to a vote that do not enjoy broad consensus, we believe that the members of the Council, particularly its permanent members, must demonstrate the necessary political will and flexibility to bridge their differences. The Council must work together to find common ground that balances the imperative of protecting innocent civilians, ensuring humanitarian access, respecting national sovereignty and effectively countering terrorism.

Equatorial Guinea urges all parties to respect the ceasefire arrangements, de-escalate hostilities and support the political process facilitated by the United Nations, in line with resolution 2254 (2015), as there can be no military solution to the conflict in Syria.
after.France:
(spoke in French): France deeply regrets the double veto cast today by the Russian Federation and China on the draft resolution presented by Belgium, Germany and Kuwait.

Once again, the Security Council has been prevented from fulfilling its primary responsibility under the Charter of the United Nations to maintain international peace and security and protect civilians. We commend the tireless and transparent efforts of the three humanitarian co-penholders, who worked relentlessly to build consensus around a purely humanitarian text aimed at ending the suffering of the civilian population in north-west Syria.

For months now, the situation in Idlib has been catastrophic. The Syrian regime and its allies have continued their relentless military offensive, characterized by indiscriminate bombardments, the destruction of civilian infrastructure, and attacks against hospitals and schools. More than 1,000 civilians have been killed, and more than 500,000 people have been forced to flee their homes, adding to the millions of already vulnerable individuals trapped in this enclave.

France has consistently stated that the fight against terrorism is a priority, but it cannot and must not be used as an excuse or a pretext to violate international humanitarian law and indiscriminately bomb civilian populations and infrastructure. Counter-terrorism operations must comply strictly with international humanitarian law; this is an absolute moral and legal obligation. The draft resolution clearly recognized that requirement, while explicitly providing an exception for operations against terrorist groups designated by the Security Council.

There is no military solution to the Syrian crisis. The military escalation in Idlib only leads to further destruction, radicalization, and instability. The only viable path forward is an immediate, verifiable, and lasting cessation of hostilities, unhindered humanitarian access, and a credible political process in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015), facilitated by the United Nations Special Envoy, starting with the swift launching of the Constitutional Committee.

Despite today’s veto, France will not abandon the Syrian people. We will continue to mobilize all our efforts, alongside our partners, to alleviate civilian suffering, demand full respect for international humanitarian law, and work toward a just and lasting political settlement in Syria.
after.Germany:
Germany deeply regrets that the draft resolution submitted by Belgium, Kuwait and Germany, which was supported by twelve members of this Council, could not be adopted today due to the negative votes of the Russian Federation and China. 

This is a profoundly disappointing outcome, above all for the more than three million civilians trapped in Idlib who live in constant fear of bombardment and displacement.

As humanitarian co-penholders, our objective in drafting this resolution was straightforward and purely humanitarian: to halt the violence, prevent an even worse catastrophe, ensure the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and secure unhindered humanitarian access. We did not act out of political motivations, but out of a fundamental responsibility to the people of north-west Syria, where months of relentless military operations by the Syrian regime and its allies have killed over a thousand civilians, displaced more than half a million people, and systematically damaged or destroyed hospitals, clinics, and schools.

We reject the claim that this draft resolution was designed to shield terrorists. The text was unequivocally clear on this point: it explicitly stated that the cessation of hostilities does not apply to military operations against individuals and groups designated as terrorists by this Security Council, including Hayat Tahrir al-Sham, Al-Qaida, and Da’esh. 

However, we must state once again, loud and clear: the fight against terrorism can never serve as a blank check or a pretext to bypass international humanitarian law. It can never justify the indiscriminate bombing of densely populated civilian areas, the destruction of civilian infrastructure, or attacks on medical facilities whose coordinates had been shared through the United Nations deconfliction mechanism. Counter-terrorism operations must strictly comply with the principles of distinction, proportionality, and precaution. The lives of innocent men, women, and children cannot simply be dismissed as collateral damage.

Today’s vetoes send a devastating signal to the people of Syria and to humanitarians risking their lives on the ground. Yet, despite this failure of the Council to act, Germany, alongside Belgium and Kuwait, will not abandon its responsibility. We will continue our steadfast efforts to alleviate the suffering of the Syrian people, uphold international humanitarian law, and demand accountability for the crimes committed in Syria.
after.Kuwait:
*(spoke in Arabic)*

At the outset, we express our deep regret at the Council’s inability today to adopt the humanitarian draft resolution submitted by Belgium, Germany and my country, Kuwait, as co-penholders of the Syrian humanitarian file, owing to the use of the veto.

Over the past four months, the world has witnessed an unprecedented humanitarian catastrophe unfolding in north-west Syria, particularly in Idlib governorate. More than 3 million civilians, the majority of whom are women and children, are trapped in an intolerable situation. Since late April, military operations have killed more than one thousand civilians, displaced over half a million people, and caused widespread destruction of civilian infrastructure, including medical facilities, schools, and markets. 

Our objective throughout the negotiations, in close coordination with our co-penholders, was purely humanitarian: to alleviate the immense suffering of innocent civilians, achieve a cessation of hostilities in Idlib, and ensure safe, rapid, unimpeded, and sustainable humanitarian access to all those in need. We engaged constructively, openly, and transparently with all Council members, taking into account many of the proposals and concerns raised, in order to preserve the unity of the Security Council on this critical humanitarian issue.

While we recognize that Hayat Tahrir al-Sham and other groups designated as terrorist organizations by the Security Council are present in Idlib, and while we fully support counter-terrorism efforts, we reiterate that the fight against terrorism does not absolve any party from its obligations under international law, particularly international humanitarian law and international human rights law. The presence of terrorist groups can never justify indiscriminate attacks against civilians, the destruction of hospitals and schools, or the collective punishment of millions of innocent people.

Today’s failure sends a discouraging message to the millions of Syrians who look to this Council for protection and hope. Nonetheless, Kuwait, along with its co-penholder partners, will not relent in its commitment to addressing the humanitarian situation in Syria and advocating for the protection of its people. We reaffirm our full respect for the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic, and we reiterate that there can be no military solution to the crisis. The only viable path forward is an inclusive, Syrian-led political process under the auspices of the United Nations, in line with resolution 2254 (2015) and the Geneva Communiqué of 2012.
after.Peru:
(spoke in Spanish): Peru voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by Belgium, Germany and Kuwait, the co-penholders on the humanitarian situation in Syria.

We deeply regret that, once again, the Security Council has been unable to reach consensus on a draft resolution whose objective was strictly humanitarian: to alleviate the immense suffering of more than 3 million civilians trapped by the hostilities in north-west Syria.

Peru reiterates its grave concern over the serious military escalation in Idlib and surrounding areas, which has caused hundreds of civilian deaths, massive displacement and the destruction of essential civilian infrastructure, including schools and medical facilities. We strongly condemn all attacks against civilians and civilian objects, which constitute serious violations of international humanitarian law.

We recognize the threat posed by terrorist groups designated by this Council, such as Hayat Tahrir al-Sham and Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant, and we reaffirm the need to combat them. However, counter-terrorism operations cannot be used to justify indiscriminate attacks or disproportionate use of force. Any action against terrorism must strictly adhere to international law, in particular international humanitarian law, and respect the principles of distinction, precaution and proportionality.

We also stress the urgent need to ensure safe, rapid, unimpeded and sustained humanitarian access to all civilians in need, as well as the protection of humanitarian and medical personnel.

Finally, Peru reiterates that there can be no military solution to the conflict in Syria. We reiterate our firm support for the United Nations-facilitated, Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process, in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015) and the Geneva communiqué, and we hope that the early establishment and convening of the Constitutional Committee will represent a decisive step towards achieving a lasting and peaceful solution to the conflict.
after.South Africa:
South Africa voted in favour of the draft resolution contained in document S/2019/756, submitted by the humanitarian co-penholders—Belgium, Germany and Kuwait. 

South Africa remains deeply concerned by the ongoing hostilities in north-west Syria, particularly in and around Idlib, and the catastrophic humanitarian impact this escalation has had on the civilian population. The loss of civilian lives, the destruction of civilian infrastructure, including schools and medical facilities, and the displacement of hundreds of thousands of people are unacceptable and require urgent and concerted action by the international community and this Council.

Our vote in favour of the draft resolution was guided by our principled stance on the protection of civilians and the absolute necessity of ensuring rapid, safe, and unhindered humanitarian access to all individuals in need. All parties to the conflict must scrupulously respect their obligations under international law, including international humanitarian law and international human rights law. The principles of distinction, proportionality and precaution must be upheld at all times.

At the same time, South Africa reiterates its condemnation of all acts of terrorism and recognizes the threat posed by Council-designated terrorist groups in Idlib, including Hayat Tahrir al-Sham. However, counter-terrorism operations cannot and must not be conducted at the expense of civilian protection or in violation of international humanitarian law. Operations against terrorist groups must be carried out with utmost care to avoid civilian casualties and further suffering.

South Africa deeply regrets that the Council was once again unable to reach consensus on such a vital humanitarian issue. The division among Council members undermines our collective ability to address the urgent needs of the Syrian people. We continue to urge all Council members to bridge their differences and work towards unity.

Finally, South Africa reaffirms that there can be no military solution to the conflict in Syria. The only sustainable path to peace is through an inclusive, Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political dialogue in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015), which fully respects the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
I thank the co-penholders — Belgium, Germany and Kuwait — for their tireless and principled efforts to find an agreement on this purely humanitarian text. The United Kingdom voted in favour of the draft resolution because we believe that the Security Council has a fundamental responsibility to act to protect civilians and halt the carnage in north-west Syria.

We are deeply disappointed, though sadly not surprised, by the decision of the Russian Federation and China to veto this draft resolution. Today marks the thirteenth time that Russia has used its veto to shield the Syrian regime and prevent this Council from taking action to relieve the immense suffering of the Syrian people. 

Twelve members of this Council voted in favour of an immediate cessation of hostilities to save lives, allow unhindered humanitarian access, and end the attacks on hospitals, schools, and medical facilities. The draft resolution made explicitly clear that counter-terrorism operations against Council-designated terrorist groups were exempt, while reaffirming what should be an indisputable principle: counter-terrorism cannot and must not be used as a carte blanche to terrorize three million civilians, bomb civilian infrastructure, and breach international humanitarian law.

Russia claims that the situation is under control and that its military campaign is directed only at terrorists. Yet the reality on the ground tells a very different story: more than half a million people displaced since April, over a thousand civilians killed, and dozens of hospitals and clinics struck by aerial bombardment. 

By vetoing today’s text, Russia and China have once again chosen to prioritize the Syrian regime’s brutal military offensive over the desperate humanitarian needs of innocent men, women, and children trapped in Idlib. This Council was established to maintain international peace and security and to protect the vulnerable. Today, two permanent members have prevented it from doing so. The United Kingdom will continue to stand with the people of Syria and work with all partners to pursue accountability and a lasting political solution in line with resolution 2254 (2015).
after.United States of America:
I thank the co-penholders—Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait—for their tireless efforts and leadership in drafting a balanced, purely humanitarian resolution aimed at stopping the slaughter in north-west Syria and protecting innocent lives.

The United States voted in favor of this resolution because the people of Idlib desperately need relief. More than three million civilians, over half of whom have already been displaced from other parts of Syria, are trapped in an escalating nightmare. Since late April, the Assad regime, backed by the Russian Federation, has relentlessly bombarded Idlib, killing more than one thousand civilians, displacing over half a million people, and systematically destroying critical civilian infrastructure, including dozens of hospitals, healthcare centers, and schools.

It is deeply shameful and tragic that Russia and China have once again chosen to use their vetoes to block Council action to halt this brutality. Today marks Russia’s thirteenth veto on Syria. By casting their vetoes today, Russia and China have chosen to provide diplomatic cover to the Assad regime as it continues its merciless campaign against its own people. 

The Council must be clear: fighting terrorism cannot and does not serve as an excuse or a blank check to slaughter innocent civilians, bomb schools, and target hospitals. Counter-terrorism operations must comply with international humanitarian law. The draft resolution made that crystal clear, reaffirming our collective commitment to defeat Security Council-designated terrorist groups while insisting on the protection of civilians. 

Today, twelve members of this Council stood together in defense of humanity, international law, and the Syrian people. Russia and China stood alone in vetoing a purely humanitarian measure. 

The United States calls on the Assad regime and Russia to immediately halt their military offensive, adhere to a genuine and durable ceasefire, grant unhindered humanitarian access, and commit to the United Nations-led political process under resolution 2254 (2015). There is no military solution to this conflict, and we will continue to stand firmly with the Syrian people.
